# privacy-gate allowlist for sigharvest (scripts/maintainer/privacy_gate.py, run by .github/workflows/ci.yml)
# Format: <path-glob> <rule-id|glob|*> [re:<regex matched against the offending line>] -- <justification>
# Keep entries narrow (prefer a re: filter) and always justified. Unused entries are reported.
# Project-specific rules come from the terms file (SIGHARVEST_PRIVACY_TERMS); entries below name them only by glob.

# --- the gate itself ------------------------------------------------------------
scripts/*privacy_gate.py * -- the gate contains the patterns it looks for

# --- public Sigma taxonomy: product names used as logsource product values ------
src/*/logsource_catalog.py vendor-* -- public Sigma logsource product names (taxonomy), not integrations
src/*/normalize.py vendor-* -- logsource product alias normalisation (public Sigma taxonomy)

# --- synthetic test data ----------------------------------------------------------
tests/* secret-url-credentials re:(?i)user:[^@]*@(?:[\w-]+\.)*(example|invalid|test|host) -- redaction tests use fake credentials on reserved domains

# --- git history ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exactly these two commits (SHA prefix, author/committer identity only); every other commit is still checked.
# Commit-scoped entries: commit:<sha-prefix, 7-40 hex>[*][:<path-glob>]; they never match tree findings.
commit:0e6ca78def:* email-commit-author -- legacy commits; history not published
commit:dc4e315ceb:* email-commit-author -- legacy commits; history not published

# --- the organisation's own public addresses ------------------------------------
# Only lines whose every address is on threat-hunting.eu (the project role address, security), or on threat-hunter.eu (the
# previous address, still in older commits: history scans must keep passing); any other
# address on the same line, a subdomain or a look-alike domain is still blocked.
* email-real re:(?i)^(?:[^@]|@threat-hunt(?:ing|er)\.eu(?![\w-]|\.[\w-]))*$ -- the project's public role address (security, on threat-hunting.eu; threat-hunter.eu only in older commits)

# --- GitHub bot identities in commit metadata ---------------------------------------
# Dependabot commits carry a "Signed-off-by: dependabot[bot]" trailer with GitHub's support address (its author and
# GitHub's web-flow committer use noreply addresses, already safe). Only that address, only in commit trailers.
<trailer> email-commit-author re:^support@github\.com$ -- Dependabot's Signed-off-by trailer (dependabot[bot], GitHub support address)

# --- co-maintainer commit identity --------------------------------------------------
# The co-maintainer (elhoim) publishes his commits under this address by choice; squash merges of his pull requests
# carry it as author. Only this exact address, only in commit author/committer/Co-authored-by metadata.
<author> email-commit-author re:^elhoim@gmail\.com$ -- co-maintainer's public commit address (his choice, accepted by the maintainers)
<committer> email-commit-author re:^elhoim@gmail\.com$ -- co-maintainer's public commit address (his choice, accepted by the maintainers)
<trailer> email-commit-author re:^elhoim@gmail\.com$ -- co-maintainer's public commit address (his choice, accepted by the maintainers)
